Pairwise IBD segments along the genome

Source: R/segments.R
ibd_segments.Rd

The stretches of genome over which two parasites are identical by descent – the detail behind the single IBD number from ibd_pairs(). A segment is a maximal stretch over which the two genomes descend from one common ancestor genome, cut at each chromosome junction, the same rows as ibd_pairs(segments = TRUE) gives for the pair; each is in both concatenated and within-chromosome coordinates.

Usage

ibd_segments(run, ids_a, ids_b, min_span = 1000)

Arguments

run

a run: a vivax_run (from run_sim() or load_run()) or the path of a run directory.

ids_a, ids_b

equal-length vectors of pedigree ids, compared position by position.

min_span

the shortest segment returned, in bp, after the cut at the junctions (a segment of exactly min_span is kept): below it a shared stretch is treated as noise, mirroring the detection floor of IBD inference.

Value

a data.table, by pair and position: pair (the position in ids_a and ids_b, from 1), a and b (as given), chrom (the PvP01 chromosome), start and end (bp within the chromosome, end exclusive), gstart and gend (bp along the concatenated genome), length (bp), mrca_id (the pedigree id of the common ancestor), mrca_time and depth (its age; see ibd_pairs()). A pair sharing nothing has no rows, and nor does a pair with a genome the tree sequence does not hold, which warns; the table's "missing" attribute lists those ids. A genome with itself is shared end to end: one row per chromosome, its own ancestor at depth 0. A pair given twice has its rows twice.

Python

The IBD and ARG functions read a run's tree sequence with Python's tskit, through the reticulate package. Either of two routes works. Automatic: with no Python chosen, reticulate sets up its own environment with tskit (>= 1.0) and numpy the first time one of these functions runs; this needs internet once. Your own Python: set RETICULATE_PYTHON to a Python that has those modules (in ~/.Renviron to keep it) before the first such call of a session. A function that cannot reach them stops with an error of class malariafwd_no_python that says what to do, and check_setup() reports what is found.

See also

plot_ibd_pair(), ibd_pairs()

Examples

run <- example_run()
rel <- load_events(run)[event_type == "hypnozoite_activation" & parent1_pedigree_id != -1][1]
ibd_segments(run, rel$pedigree_id, rel$parent1_pedigree_id)   # all 14 chromosomes shared
